 This W.P Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of
The Constitution Of India Praying To Declare That
The Acquisition Proceedings In Respect Of The
Schedule Lands Belonging To The Petitioner Under
The Preliminary Notification Dated 23.3.1988 Vide Ann-
E And The Final Notification Dated 19.10.1994 Vide
Ann-F As Having Lapsed And Become Void In So Far As
Hands Of The Petitioner Concern And Etc.,
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing
In 'B' Group, This Day, Order

WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER

In this writ petition, the petitioner is assailing the Preliminary Notification dated 23.03.1988 (Annexure-E) and Final Notification dated 19.10.1994 (Annexure-F) as having become lapsed insofar as the land of the petitioner is concerned.

The relevant facts for adjudication of the writ petition are that, the petitioner herein has purchased the scheduled land as per the registered sale deed dated 05.04.2014 from its previous predecessors in title Smt.Poornima S.Nayak and Smt. Vishalakshi S.Nayak represented by their GPA holder-Sri.A.M.Ramaraju.
It is the case of the petitioner that, the revenue entries were mutated in favour of the petitioner and the petitioner is in possession of the schedule property.
3. It is the contention of the petitioner that, the land in question was not the subject matter of any acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondents.

The petitioner has further stated that, the petitioner came to know about the issuance of the Preliminary Notification dated 23.03.1988 and the Final Notification dated 19.10.1994 and the notification issued by the respondent-authorities under Section 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, with regard to taking possession of the schedule property as per Annexure-E, F and G, respectively.

4. It is the specific contention of the petitioner that, since the acquisition proceedings, has not reached the logical NC: 2024:KHC:43803 end on account of not taking possession, as well as the Sri. sentences.text: Final Notification issued on 19.10.1994, which held to be invalid by this Court in WP.No.32881/1994, the respondent-BDA ought to have issued a fresh notification with regard to the acquisition of land of the erstwhile owners of the petitioner and in this regard, it is contended in the writ petition that the entire impugned notifications are liable to be quashed in view of the judgment of this Court in R.K.SHIVAGIRI NAIDU AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2011 KAR 3657.

entities.text: R.K.SHIVAGIRI NAIDU AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND OTHERS reported in ILR 2011 KAR 3657
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this writ petition.

5. Heard Sri. B.S.Radhanandan, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri. Ravindranath.B,
learned AGA for respondent No.1 and Sri. B.Vachan, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3.
6.

Sri. B.S.Radhanandan, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, vehemently contended that this Court, in WP.No.32881/1994 disposed of on 26.09.1996, has quashed the Final Notification dated 19.10.1994 (Annexure-F) and in that view of the matter, any action that has been taken by the respondent-BDA in furtherance of the same, would void ab NC: 2024:KHC:43803 initio unless a fresh notification has been issued in furtherance of the order passed by this Court in the above writ petition.

He also refers to the various judgments of this Court, relating to the fact that the scheme of the respondent-BDA has been lapsed under Section 27 of the BDA-respondent (For short, BDA Act),
as the respondent-BDA has not implemented the scheme substantially as required under law and accordingly, sought for interference of this Court.
7.

It is also argued by Sri.B.S.Radhanandan, learned counsel, by referring to the judgment of this Court in WP.No.11022-24/2011 and connected writ petitions disposed of on 08.08.2012, argued that, even though the petitioner- vendors have challenged the acquisition proceedings and were unsuccessful and the said aspect is not a ground to dismiss the writ petition on the ground of resjudicata and therefore, he contended that the petitioner herein has a fresh cause of action to challenge the impugned notification on the ground of lapsing of the acquisition proceedings.

He also referred to the recent judgment of this Court in WP.No.55159/2014, disposed of by this Court on 19.07.2022 and argued that the finding as to lapsing of scheme in the proceedings would be restricted to the NC: 2024:KHC:43803 petitioner herein and therefore, contended that the situation of the petitioner herein is similar to that of the plaintiff in a suit for injunction, whenever there is any fresh cause of action to file the suit for injunction and therefore, sought for interference of this Court.

8. Per contra, Sri.B.Vachan, learned counsel appearing for the respondent, raised a preliminary objection relating to the maintainability of the writ petition on the ground that, the vendors of the petitioner herein, in the case of SMT.VISHALAKSHI S.NAYAK AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND OTHERS reported in 2012 SCC Online KAR 6989 challenged the very same notification dated 19.10.1994 before this Court and this Court has considered the entire case on merits and dismissed the petition.

9. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, having taken note of the undisputed fact that the vendor-petitioner herein has challenged the very same final notification in WP.No.33578- 579/2010 and the said writ petition was dismissed by this Court by order dated 03.04.2012 in the case of SMT.VISHALAKSHI S.NAYAK (supra).

Paragraph Nos.2 to 3 of the said case held as follows:
"2. Petitioners have purchased property bearing Sy. No. 45/2 measuring 6 acres 5 guntas of Kothanur village, Uttarahalli hobli, Bangalore South taluk from its earlier owner Munirajappa @ Muninanja Reddy and his son Sri Chandrakumar through registered sale deed dated 29.8.1986.

On 23.3.1988 the Bangalore Development Authority ('BDA' for short) issued preliminary notification acquiring the aforesaid land alongwith various other properties for formation of 'Jayaprakashnarayan Nagar 8th Stage' lay-out.

Though the petitioners were the owners of the property in question and though khatha was changed in their names, still the BDA notified the name of Munirajappa, the name of the erstwhile owner as the khathedar of the land in question.
Thereafter the final notification came to be issued in the month of October- 1994 as per Annexure-B in the name of Munirajappa.
Thereafter award came to be passed.

By the time, the award came NC: 2024:KHC:43803 to be passed,
Munirajappa had expired.
His son Mr. M. Chandrakumar suppressing the sale made by his father in favour of the petitioners withdrew the compensation deposited by the BDA.

On coming to know that the compensation is withdrawn by Mr. Chandrakumar,
the petitioners filed O.S. No. 5627/2003 before the Civil Court for declaration and consequential relief.
The said suit ended in compromise.
Mr. Chandakumar agreed to return the compensation amount which was received by him.
Accordingly, he addressed a letter to BDA returning the compensation amount received by him by way of Demand Draft in favour of BDA.
However the BDA did not accept the compensation and directed Chandrakumar to deposit the same in the Civil Court as he had withdrawn the compensation from the Civil Court.
The Endorsement so issued by BDA was questioned by Mr. Chandrakumar in W.P. No. 21641/2005 before this Court.
The petitioners herein also filed W.P. No. 5753/2006 before this Court questioning the acquisition notifications and also for quashing the endorsement.
Both the writ petitions were dismissed and the acquisition notifications became final.
After dismissal of W.P. No. 21641/2005 c/w W.P. 5753/2006 by this Court on 17.9.2007, the compensation is re- deposited by Mr. Chandrakumar in the Civil Court.

3. Relying upon the Judgment of this Court in W.P. No. 46002/99 and connected matters disposed of on 31.3.2004, learned counsel for the petitioners contends that the impugned acquisition notifications are liable to be quashed inasmuch as the learned Single Judge in the said writ petitions had already quashed the entire preliminary as well as final notifications.

He further submits that the judgment of the Sri. B.R. Pradeep Kumar vs The State Of Karnataka on 30 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140196283/
4 learned Single Judge in W.P. No. 46002/99 and connected matters is affirmed by the Division Bench of this Court on 31.10.2011 in W.A. No. 3825/2005 and connected matters.

sentences.text: He further submits that possession of the property in question is not taken by the BDA and the same remains with the petitioners; that the petitioners have formed private lay-out and have sold certain of the sites NC: 2024:KHC:43803 to the third parties, who in turn have constructed the houses; such persons who have constructed the houses are shown lenlency by BDA by de- notifying their lands.
On these and other grounds, the petitioners pray for quashing the acquisition notifications.

Sri G.S. Kannur, learned advocate for the BDA opposes the writ petitions contending that the petitioners had already approached this Court by filing the writ petitions challenging the acquisition notifications, but said writ petitions came to be withdrawn and consequently the acquisition has become final.

He further submits that though the preliminary notification was issued in the name of the erstwhile owner Munirajappa, the petitioners herein had filed statement of objections to the preliminary notification and have opposed the acquisition notification.
After considering the statement of objections, the final notification came to be issued.

He further submits that the possession of the property in question is taken as far back as on 28.4.1997 and as the petitioners knew very well about the acquisition proceedings,
it is not open for them to question the acquisition notifications by filing these writ petitions for the second time."
10.

On perusal of the aforementioned order passed by this Court would indicate that there was a dispute raised by the erstwhile owners of the petitioners in OS.No.5627/2003 with regard to apportionment of compensation and the said suit was ended in compromise and thereafter, it appears that the petitioner herein has purchased the aforementioned land.
It is also to be noted that the order passed by this Court in WP.No.33578-79/2010, was confirmed by this Court in - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:43803 WA.No.1848-49/2012 disposed of on 15.03.2013.

In the light of the aforementioned aspect as the vendor's of the petitioner herein have suffered an order before the Learned Single Judge, which came to be confirmed by the Division Bench of this Court as referred to above and also taking into account the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of DELHI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY Vs. MANPREET SINGH AND OTHERS in reported in 2023 SCC Online SC 29, at paragraph Nos.6 to 8 held as follows:
"6. At the outset, it is required to be noted that it was the specific case on behalf of the appellants before the High Court that the original writ petitioner is a subsequent purchaser, who has acquired the right, title or interest in the land in the year 2018.
The original writ petitioner was not the recorded owner at the time when the award with respect to the land in quest ion under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1894") was issued.

sentences.text:
it appears that before the High Court, the original writ petitioner claimed the right,
title or interest on the basis of the Assignment Deed of 2015.
In the present case, the notification under Section 4 of the Act, 1894 was issued on 25.11.1980 and the award was declared on 05.06.1987.
Therefore, the short question, which is posed for the consideration of this Court is:-

Whether the original writ petitioner being a subsequent purchaser had locus to challenge the acquisition and/or lapsing of the acquisition?
7. The aforesaid issued in now not res integra in view of the Three Judge Bench decision of this Court in the case of Shiv Kumar (supra), which has been subsequently followed by another Bench of this Court in the cases of Godfrey Philips (I) Ltd.
(supra) and Pawan - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:43803 Kumar (supra).

The decision of this Court in the case of Shiv Kumar (supra)
is a Three Judge Bench decision by which a contrary view taken by the Two Judge Bench of this Court in the case of Government (NCT of Delhi) V.Manav Dharam Trust, (2017) 6 SCC 751 has not been accepted and is found to be not a good law.

entities.text: Government (NCT of Delhi) V.Manav Dharam Trust, (2017) 6 SCC 751
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That thereafter after following the Three Judge Bench decision in the case of Shiv Kumar (supra) in the cases of Godfrey Philips (I) Ltd. (supra) and Pawan Kumar (supra), this Court has subsequently observed and held that a subsequent purchaser has no locus to challenge the acquisition proceedings/lapsing of the acquisition under the Act, 2013.

8. In that view of the matter, the High Court has committed a serious error in entertaining the writ petition at the instance of the respondent No.1 herein- original writ petitioner and has materially erred in declaring that the acquisition with respect to the land in question is deemed to have lapsed under Section 24 (2) of the Act, 2013 in a writ petition filed by the respondent No.1 herein-original writ petitioner, who is a subsequent purchaser.

Under the circumstances and on that ground alone,
the impugned common judgment and order passed by the High Court is required to be quashed and set-aside."

11. It is categorically held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the High Court has committed an error in entertaining the writ petition, wherein the writ petitioner being a subsequent purchaser and no locus standi to challenge the acquisition or lapsing of the acquisition.

12. In that view of the matter, following the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
I am of the view that the petitioner herein, being a subsequent purchaser has no - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:43803 locus standi to challenge the acquisition proceedings including urging the ground relating lapsing of the case, which has already been concluded at the hands of petitioners filed by the vendor's of writ petitioners.
